LESSON: WORK: GOD WORKED

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation 1.1 Work 8 2.0 The Bible 2.1 Christian Moral Values 10 2.2 Kings David 
Topic 1.1: Work: God Worked

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Work: God Worked. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you work hard as a Christian?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss virtues related to Christian work ethics
2. demonstrate a positive attitude towards work in daily activities

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WORK: GOD WORKED
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Work: God Worked helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: WORK: GOD WORKED
Study Work: God Worked like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Discuss virtues related to Christian work ethics

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss virtues related to Christian work ethics. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss virtues related to Christian work ethics.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Work: God Worked” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss virtues related to Christian work ethics. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Demonstrate a positive attitude towards work in daily activities

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate a positive attitude towards work in daily activities. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate a positive attitude towards work in daily activities.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Work: God Worked in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate a positive attitude towards work in daily activities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Work: God Worked is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Work: God Worked” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: discuss virtues related to Christian work ethics)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Work: God Worked in your own words. (skill: demonstrate a positive attitude towards work in daily activities)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Work: God Worked to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss virtues related to Christian work ethics.
3. Practise this skill: demonstrate a positive attitude towards work in daily activities.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Work: God Worked from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Work: God Worked: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Work: God Worked?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you work hard as a Christian?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Work: God Worked means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss virtues related to Christian work ethics.
5. Be able to: demonstrate a positive attitude towards work in daily activities.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
